text: {"lessons":["I sold Stock D early because its gain felt worth locking in, then sold more after it had risen further; a gain alone is not a reason to sell, so I should use a consistent plan rather than react to the urge to take profits.","Selling Stock A, C and D while the account was down may have been driven by wanting to secure gains; I should judge each position on its own instead of letting account losses or small wins dictate trades.","Stock D’s later rise does not prove I could have predicted it. I should avoid judging decisions only by what prices did afterward and remember that past moves do not forecast future ones."]}
